briefs.label: Morning Brief
briefs.title: Michigan Cannabis Digs In as DEA, Psychedelics and M&A Signal a National Turning Point
briefs.top: Michigan's legal market is proving sturdier than the 24% wholesale tax doomsayers predicted, with steady demand, fresh brand launches and a governor's race now putting tax relief on the ballot. Nationally, the DEA is actively pushing marijuana toward Schedule III, Compass Pathways just cleared its second Phase 3 psilocybin hurdle, and a wave of M&A — including a $272M bid for Aurora Cannabis — shows real capital betting on the sector's next chapter.

local.text: Michigan's cannabis market remains one of the largest in the country, with July sales hitting $260.6 million on more than 30 million units sold; rock-bottom average item prices of $8.65 — the lowest of any major U.S. market — are keeping consumer traffic strong even as year-over-year revenue cools slightly.

Michigan's GOP gubernatorial nominee John James is campaigning on rolling back the 24% wholesale tax, arguing in his 'Freedom Agenda' that it 'drives up prices, gives illegal operators a competitive edge, and has already fallen far short of revenue projections' — putting real political weight behind industry relief ahead of November.

Detroit's Best in Grass Michigan awards show landed at the Royal Oak Music Theatre, giving statewide brands like Hytek, Mi Loud, Wojo Co., Pleasantrees and Nura Premium Cannabis a real shot at consumer-driven buzz and new retail traffic in a crowded shelf-space market.

Michigan brand Intrinsic — the relaunched former Choice Labs and Glorious — debuted as a new premium statewide processor built on 'heritage, craftsmanship, scale and a commitment to quality,' a bet that consolidation-era Michigan still has room for fresh, well-capitalized entrants.

On the tax fight itself, Treasury has given operators real breathing room: businesses only need 'good-faith' quarterly payments through 2026, and Treasurer Rachael Eubanks says the state is 'providing relief from penalties and interest for businesses that make good-faith quarterly payments' while the wholesale tax's constitutionality is litigated on appeal.

national.text: DEA lawyers are now formally on record telling the administrative law judge overseeing rescheduling that the evidence from the 11-day hearing shows marijuana 'no longer meets the requirements for the nation's most restrictive drug category,' urging a move to Schedule III.

The DEA released the full corrected 2,533-page transcript of the rescheduling hearing, capturing government lawyers arguing on the record that 'marijuana can no longer remain in Schedule I' — a milestone that sets up a judge's recommendation in the coming months.

Compass Pathways' second Phase 3 trial hit its primary endpoint, with two fixed doses of COMP360 psilocybin producing a 'highly statistically significant reduction in symptom severity' for treatment-resistant depression — the company says it's on track for commercial launch readiness by the end of 2026.

Compass Pathways is now partnering with the U.S. Department of Veterans Affairs on a multi-site randomized trial testing COMP360 psilocybin for treatment-resistant depression and PTSD in veterans, donating the study drug across five VA sites including Birmingham, Portland and Seattle.

Consolidation is turning into real capital deployment: Curaleaf has launched an unsolicited $272 million takeover bid for Aurora Cannabis, Vireo Growth is acquiring Planet 13 in an all-stock deal, and Tilray just posted record FY2026 revenue — signs that bigger players see growth ahead, not just distress.
